verdict.rationale: Vercel's docs and probes describe a unified platform (git push to deploy, isolated containers for production workloads, gradual rollouts, instant rollback) suggesting a consistent deployment model from prototype to production, and the llms.txt explicitly frames Vercel as scaling 'web applications and AI workloads' on one platform. However, community evidence shows scaling introduces real friction — e.g. needing to 'contact sales' for enterprise-tier secure DB connections, unexpected $10k bills from undetected scale/DDoS events, and users citing this as a reason to migrate off Vercel entirely — which undercuts the 'no rearchitecting/migrating' promise at scale. Missing for 10: independent case studies of apps scaling seamlessly from prototype to massive traffic without plan/architecture changes, and no rebuttal to the enterprise-gating/cost-surprise complaints.
